correctness.rationale: The 2-cycle equations reduce bijectively to sin(Ls)cos(cd)=0 and d=cos(Ls)sin(cd) with d in (0,1]. In 3<a<1+2pi, 0<cd<pi, yielding exactly central phase 2*pi*m and (only above a=1+pi) two split phases. The strictly increasing theta/sin(theta) gives central uniqueness. The Schur inequalities for J(cos theta) give the unique finite attracting window; for side cycles their characteristic polynomial at lambda=1 is strictly negative, proving a multiplier above one. The analytic proof includes all cases and endpoints. Reconstructed transitions and Floquet traces/determinants were also checked directly.

value.rationale: The naturally symmetric offset-reproducing map has an infinite discrete lattice of primitive-two-cycle states. The exact phase diagram detects a sharp gain with three coexisting cycles per period cell and a distinct upper stability threshold, not only illustrative trajectories. The two new side cycles are intrinsically unstable but split at a square-root rate while the central cycle becomes an attracting sink on a nonempty parameter interval. This supplies a motivated complete finite-per-cell invariant and clear local basin candidates for a published dynamics model, not a parameter-renaming or numerical graph.
